overview: The 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act created a competitive grant program, run by the Interior Department's Bureau of Reclamation, for large water recycling and reuse projects in Western states, such as plants that treat wastewater so it can be used again. That program was set to expire after five years. This bill extends it to ten years and lets projects already under construction when it ends continue to be covered. It also allows grants to pay for feasibility studies, the early engineering and cost reviews that come before planning and construction, and changes one of the numerical conditions grant recipients must meet. As of September 17, 2026, a Senate committee had approved it with changes and it was placed on the Senate calendar for possible floor action.
for: Supporters say drought-stricken Western communities need more time and flexibility to plan and build large recycling projects, which take years, and that recycled water is a reliable new supply.
against: Critics say extending the program keeps federal money flowing to large, costly local projects, and that communities that benefit should rely more on their own funding.
